page: Microsoft Azure D160alds_v7 is a compute-oriented virtual machine from the Daldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 80 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores with a base clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptography extensions like AES and SHA_NI. The system is configured with 320.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core, and includes 9449 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the D160alds_v7 consistently ranks in the top tier (top 10%) across multiple compute and memory metrics. It achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as Geekbench multi-core and software compilation tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached speeds reaching 14559.08 GB/sec and uncached write speeds at 209.95 GB/sec. Database and web serving capabilities are also in the top tier, as demonstrated by 202.38 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 112.41 GB/sec. For machine learning tasks, prompt processing for small and medium LLMs falls into the top tier, though text generation for smaller models drops to the middle 50%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high compute density and massive local NVMe storage, making it a viable option for workloads requiring high-throughput local disk access without the overhead of external storage. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio represents a tradeoff for memory-bound applications. This hardware profile is best suited for compute-intensive workloads, large-scale database operations, software compilation pipelines, and high-throughput web serving.

It features 320.0 GB of RAM and 9449 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server delivers top-tier performance in multi-core processing, software compilation, and database operations, as evidenced by its top 10% ranking in stress-ng, Geekbench, and Redis benchmarks. While its low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive tasks, its high compute density and massive local storage make it highly efficient for compute-heavy workloads, large-scale database hosting, and high-throughput web serving.
